competency_fulfillment.rationale: Genuine addition word problems and pictorial problems appear, e.g. seed 42's 'There are 1 resin in one basket and 10 resin in another basket. How many resin are there in all?' and seed 55's frog-emoji visual, both matching 'solve problems... involving addition' directly.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Both the 'given orally' and 'in pictures' sub-cases are present, but the competency's 'sums up to 100 without regrouping' scope is barely reached -- the largest addend across all eight samples is 12 (seed 44's ribbons), and no sample sums two 2-digit numbers or approaches even half of the stated 100 ceiling.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Seed 45 repeats a singular/plural grammar mismatch, 'One basket has 3 water bottles. Another basket has 1 water bottles...', and seed 50's 'merchandise shirts' phrasing remains stilted, both potentially confusing for an early Grade 1 reader.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Framings span object word problems (resin at seed 42, ribbons at seed 44, water bottles at seed 45, merchandise shirts at seed 50), a counting-up number-line narration (seeds 43, 46, 72), a pictorial frog-emoji model (seed 55), and error-detection (seed 50).

competency_alignment.rationale: Every sample, including the counting-up narration at seed 46 ('Start at 1. Count up 3 more. What number do you land on?'), is a genuine addition-in-context scenario matching this competency's word-problem scope.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The largest sum across all eight samples is 13 (seed 44's '12 ribbons... 1 ribbon... how many in all'), nowhere near the stated ceiling of 100, and no sample exercises the larger two-digit-plus-two-digit range this Quarter 2 node is meant to add beyond its Quarter 1 counterpart.
